text:
S: 28M boda rider c/o fever with chills and rigors x3/7, frontal headache, generalised body aches, poor appetite. No vomiting, no convulsions, no confusion. No cough. Last antimalarial >1 yr ago.
O: Alert, T 38.9, PR 104, BP 118/76, RR 18, SpO2 98%. Not pale, no jaundice. Mild splenic tip. Chest clear.
Ix: BS for MPS: P. falciparum trophozoites seen, ~1+ (low density). Hb 13.4.
A: Uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
P: Coartem 80/480 1 tab BD x3/7 with fatty meal, Panadol 1g TDS PRN, oral fluids. Return if vomiting, drowsiness or not better in 48h.
32F ?malaria - fever, sore body, runny nose and mild cough x2/7. T 37.9, throat mildly inj, chest clear. mRDT NEG. Dx viral URTI, malaria excluded. Panadol, warm fluids, review PRN.

Doctor: What brings you in today?
Patient: My chest is tight since last night, I'm wheezing, and the inhaler is not helping like before.
Doctor: You've had asthma since childhood, right? How many puffs of the blue inhaler have you used?
Patient: Yes, since I was small. Maybe eight or ten puffs since morning. The cold weather started it.
Doctor: Any fever or yellow sputum?
Patient: No fever. Just a dry cough.
Doctor: Your saturation is ninety-four percent, you're speaking in full sentences, and I can hear wheeze on both sides. Peak flow is about sixty percent of your best. This is an asthma attack, moderate. We'll give salbutamol nebs now, three back to back with ipratropium, and a short course of prednisolone forty milligrams for five days.
Patient: Okay.
Doctor: After the nebs we reassess. Use the inhaler with the spacer, and start your brown steroid inhaler again every day. If you get breathless at rest, come back immediately.

24F, teacher. Fever x10/7, was treated for malaria at a chemist 1/52 ago (AL) without improvement. Now persistent step-ladder fever, headache, abdo discomfort, constipation, anorexia.
O/E: T 39.2, PR 88 (relative bradycardia), coated tongue, mild diffuse abdo tenderness, no guarding, no peritonism. No rash.
Ix: BS no MPS x2. Blood culture (sent 3/7 ago at triage): Salmonella Typhi isolated, sensitive to azithromycin and ceftriaxone, resistant to cipro.
Imp: Enteric fever - typhoid, culture confirmed. Previous "malaria" was likely misdiagnosis.
Plan: Azithromycin 1g OD x7/7, Panadol, oral fluids, hand hygiene counselling. Review day 3; if any abdominal pain worsening or bleeding PR -> come immediately (risk of perforation).

27F c/o vulval itch + thick white curd-like discharge x5/7, finished Augmentin last wk for tonsillitis. LMP 2/52 ago, UPT neg. O/E: vulval erythema, white plaques on vaginal wall, no odour. Dx vaginal thrush. Clotrimazole pessary 500mg stat + cream; fluconazole 150mg stat.

Doctor: Hello mama, what's the problem with the little one?
Patient: She is six. She has had small itchy spots since yesterday, they started on the tummy and back and now some on the face. Some have water inside.
Doctor: Any fever?
Patient: Mild fever yesterday. She is eating fine. Her classmate had the same thing last week.
Doctor: I can see spots at different stages, some red bumps, some blisters, some crusting. The chest is clear, she's alert and none look infected. This is chickenpox, and it looks uncomplicated. Give calamine lotion and the antihistamine syrup at night for the itch, Panadol for fever. Please don't give Brufen. Keep her home from school until all the spots have crusted, about a week.
Patient: Can her baby brother get it?
Doctor: Yes, he might. Watch him, and come back if either of them has difficulty breathing, spots that become red and painful with pus, or she becomes drowsy.

55M, known hypertensive on amlodipine 10mg, c/o productive cough x5/7, fever, R-sided pleuritic chest pain, breathlessness on walking.
O/E: T 38.4, RR 26, SpO2 92% RA, PR 108, BP 132/84. Bronchial breathing and coarse crackles R base.
CXR: R lower zone opacity.
CRB-65: 0. OK for outpatient Rx with close review.
Dx: Community-acquired pneumonia, R lower zone.
Plan: Amoxicillin 1g TDS + azithromycin 500mg OD x5/7, Panadol, continue amlodipine. Review in 48h, earlier if worse breathing. Sputum for GeneXpert sent (cough with fever) - await.

9yo boy, itchy painful swellings on toes both feet x2/52, black dot centres, walks barefoot. Multiple embedded fleas noted R big toe, L 3rd/4th toes. No cellulitis. Dx jiggers. Removal under aseptic technique, KMnO4 soaks, shoes advised, household spraying.

C/O: 38M, cough >3/52 productive, night sweats, wt loss ~6kg in 2 months, intermittent fever. Works in a crowded matatu stage. No known TB contact. HIV test today (PITC): negative.
O/E: Wasted, BMI 17.2, T 37.8, SpO2 96%. Crepitations L upper zone.
Ix: Sputum GeneXpert: MTB detected, low; RIF resistance not detected. CXR: L upper lobe infiltrates with small cavity.
Imp: Bacteriologically confirmed pulmonary TB, new patient, drug-susceptible.
Plan: Notify, register in TIBU. Start 2RHZE/4RH weight-band dosing. Nutritional support. Contact tracing for household. Counsel on adherence and cough hygiene. Review 2/52, sputum at end of month 2.

Doctor: Good morning. So the boy is how old?
Patient: Eight years. He's had a sore throat for three days and fever, and now he won't eat because it hurts to swallow.
Doctor: Any cough or runny nose?
Patient: No cough. No flu.
Doctor: Let me look. Open wide, say ah. His tonsils are swollen, red, with white patches on both sides, and the glands under his jaw are tender. Temperature thirty-eight point six.
Patient: Is it serious?
Doctor: It's acute tonsillitis. We don't have the rapid strep test here, so I'll treat it with amoxicillin syrup for ten days, plus Panadol for the pain and fever. Give soft foods and lots of fluids. Finish the full ten days even when he feels better.
Patient: Okay, doctor.
Doctor: If he drools, can't open his mouth or can't drink at all, bring him back the same day.

Comprehensive Care Clinic review. 41F, HIV dx 2019, on TLD 1 tab OD, also known hypertensive on nifedipine.
S: Here for 3-month refill. Feels well. No cough, fever, night sweats or wt loss (ICF negative). Good adherence, no missed doses. No new rashes, no oral sores.
O: Wt 68kg (stable), BP 136/86. No lymphadenopathy, no oral thrush, skin clear.
Ix: VL 6 months ago <50 copies/mL (suppressed). CD4 not done.
A: HIV, WHO clinical stage 1, virally suppressed on TLD; HTN controlled.
P: Refill TLD x3/12, nifedipine refill. Repeat VL due next visit. Continue condom use. Return 3/12.

14yo boy from Kwale, c/o blood in urine at end of micturition x1/12, swims in the river. ?UTI. Urinalysis: RBC +++, nitrites neg, leuc neg. Urine microscopy (midday sample): terminal-spined ova seen. Dx urinary bilharzia. Praziquantel 40mg/kg stat. Avoid river contact.

68M, ex-smoker (40 pack-yrs), known COPD on salbutamol inhaler PRN, uses charcoal jiko indoors.
c/o increased breathlessness x4/7, cough with increased volume of green sputum, now breathless on walking to the toilet. No chest pain. No fever.
O/E: Pursed-lip breathing, RR 26, SpO2 89% RA -> 93% on 2L O2. Hyperinflated chest, scattered wheeze and prolonged expiration, no focal crackles. PR 102.
Ix: CXR hyperinflation, no consolidation. RBS 6.1.
Imp: Acute exacerbation of COPD (increased dyspnoea, sputum volume and purulence).
Plan: Salbutamol + ipratropium nebs, prednisolone 40mg OD x5/7, amoxicillin-clav 625mg TDS x5/7. Inhaler technique reviewed. Refer for spirometry when stable. Advise ventilation away from jiko smoke.

Doctor: Tell me what happened with the baby.
Patient: He is two years. Since yesterday he has watery diarrhoea, maybe seven times, and he vomited three times. There is no blood in the stool.
Doctor: Any fever?
Patient: Yes, he was hot last night. His cousin who stays with us had the same diarrhoea two days ago.
Doctor: Is he drinking?
Patient: He drinks eagerly, like he's very thirsty.
Doctor: His eyes are a bit sunken, he's restless but alert, and the skin pinch goes back slowly. So he has some dehydration. This looks like an infectious gastroenteritis, probably viral since his cousin had it too. We'll give ORS here in the clinic over four hours, about six hundred mls, and zinc tablets for ten days.
Patient: Does he need antibiotics?
Doctor: No, there's no blood in the stool, so antibiotics won't help. Keep breastfeeding and feeding him. If he can't drink, vomits everything, or you see blood, come back immediately.

7yo girl, itchy scaly patches on scalp with hair breakage x1/12, sibling similar. Grey scaly alopecic patches occipital, no boggy swelling, no pus. Dx tinea capitis. Griseofulvin 20mg/kg/d x6/52, ketoconazole shampoo, don't share combs.

Hx: 45M, livestock keeper from Narok, c/o on-and-off fevers x6/52 with drenching night sweats, low back pain and pain in both knees, fatigue. Drinks unboiled milk from his herd; some goats have aborted recently. Treated twice for malaria at local dispensary without relief.
Exam: T 38.1, mild hepatosplenomegaly, no joint effusion. Not pale.
Labs: BS neg. Brucella antibody (agglutination) titre 1:320 positive. FHG: mild leucopenia.
Assessment: Brucellosis.
Plan: Doxycycline 100mg BD x6/52 + rifampicin 600mg OD x6/52 (TB screen negative - no cough). Advise boiling milk, protective gloves at kidding. Review 2/52.

Doctor: Karibu. What's troubling you?
Patient: My nose is blocked and there's thick yellow stuff coming out for about ten days now. My face here, below the eyes, is painful, especially when I bend down.
Doctor: Did it start as a cold?
Patient: Yes, it was a cold at first, then got better for two days, and then worse again with fever.
Doctor: Any swelling around the eyes or problems with your vision?
Patient: No, nothing like that.
Doctor: You're tender over both cheekbones, there's pus in the nose, temperature thirty-eight. This is acute sinusitis, likely bacterial since it got worse again after improving. I'll give you amoxicillin-clavulanate for seven days, a saline nasal spray, and a steroid nasal spray. Steam inhalation helps too.
Patient: Okay.
Doctor: If you get eye swelling, severe headache or double vision, come back straight away.

S: 33M c/o loose stools with blood and mucus x5/7, 6-8 times daily, lower abdo cramping, tenesmus. Low-grade fever. Drinks borehole water. No recent travel.
O: T 37.6, mild dehydration (dry mucosa), tender L iliac fossa, no guarding. BP 112/70.
Ix: Stool microscopy: E. histolytica trophozoites with ingested RBCs seen. Occult blood +.
A: Amoebic dysentery.
P: Metronidazole (Flagyl) 800mg TDS x7/7 then diloxanide furoate 500mg TDS x10/7. ORS. Avoid alcohol with Flagyl. Boil drinking water. Review if not better 72h.

11yo boy, painful swelling both sides of jaw in front of the ears x2/7, fever, pain on chewing. Not vaccinated vs mumps. Testes normal, no headache/neck stiffness, abdo soft. Dx mumps. Panadol, soft diet, isolate from school x5/7.

42F c/o cough x10/7, initially dry now productive of clear-white sputum, mild chest soreness from coughing. Had runny nose and sore throat at onset. No fever now, no breathlessness, no wt loss, no night sweats. Non-smoker. Known diabetic on metformin, RBS today 8.2.
O/E: T 36.9, RR 16, SpO2 98%, few scattered rhonchi clearing with cough, no crackles, no bronchial breathing.
Imp: Acute bronchitis, likely post-viral. No features of pneumonia.
Plan: No antibiotics. Honey/warm fluids, Panadol PRN, cough expected to settle over 2-3 wks. Continue metformin. If cough >3 wks, fever or wt loss -> return for TB screen.

28M boda boda rider. c/o epigastric burning pain x2/52, worse when he skips meals, eases after eating. Occasional nausea, no vomiting. No haematemesis, no black stools, no wt loss. No NSAID use, alcohol rarely, non-smoker.
O/E: Gen cond good, not pale. Abd soft, mild epigastric tenderness, no guarding, no masses.
Ix: H. pylori stool Ag NEGATIVE. Hb 14.6.
Imp: Gastritis.
Plan: Omeprazole 20mg BD x4/52, Relcer gel 10ml TDS PRN, regular meals, avoid long fasting. Review in 4/52, OGD referral if no response or alarm features.

34F c/o fever on and off, burning on passing urine and increased frequency x3/7. Thought it was malaria, took nothing.
LMP 2/52 ago, UPT negative. No vaginal discharge. No loin pain, no rigors, no vomiting.
O/E: T 37.9, PR 92, BP 118/76. No renal angle tenderness. Abd soft.
mRDT: negative.
Urinalysis: leucocytes +++, nitrites +, blood +, protein trace.
Dx: UTI. Malaria excluded.
Plan: Nitrofurantoin 100mg BD x5/7, urine c/s sent, oral fluids, Panadol 1g TDS PRN. Return if loin pain, vomiting or fever persists.

62F, known HTN on amlodipine 5mg (BP 138/84 today). B/L knee pain x2yrs, worse on stairs, AM stiffness <30 min, crepitus ++, no effusion, no deformity. Imp: OA knees. Plan: Celecoxib 200mg OD x2/52, quads exercises, wt reduction, review 6/52.

19F student, c/o itchy raised rash all over the body since yesterday morning. Individual lumps come and go within a few hours. No new drugs, no new foods or cosmetics, no insect bites. No lip or tongue swelling, no difficulty breathing, no abdominal pain. First episode.
O/E: Alert, SpO2 99% RA, BP 112/70. Multiple raised erythematous wheals on trunk and both arms, blanching. No angioedema. Chest clear.
Dx: Acute urticaria, trigger not identified.
Plan: Cetirizine 10mg BD x7/7, calamine lotion. Advised to return immediately if lip swelling or breathing difficulty.

Doctor: Karibu. Mum says you've been missing school. Tell me what happens.
Patient: Every month when my period starts I get very bad pain here in the lower tummy. The first two days I can't even stand.
Doctor: When did your periods start?
Patient: When I was thirteen. I'm seventeen now. The pain has been there almost from the start.
Doctor: Are they regular? Heavy?
Patient: Every month, about five days. Not very heavy, maybe three pads a day.
Doctor: Any pain between periods, any discharge, pain when passing urine?
Patient: No.
Doctor: And I have to ask, are you sexually active?
Patient: No.
Doctor: Okay. Tummy is soft, nothing tender today. What you have is painful periods, we call it primary dysmenorrhoea. It's common and it's treatable. I'll give you mefenamic acid, Ponstan. Start it the day before you expect your period and take it with food for the first two to three days. A hot water bottle helps too. If it's not better after three months, come back and we'll do a scan.

41M, known asthmatic on Seretide, stable. c/o toothache lower left back tooth x5/7, now swelling of the left side of the face/jaw x2/7, can't chew.
O/E: T 37.8. Left submandibular facial swelling, warm, tender. Mouth opening adequate, no trismus. Floor of mouth soft, tongue not elevated, no drooling. Grossly carious lower left first molar, TTP +++, buccal vestibular swelling.
Dx: Dental (periapical) abscess lower left first molar with facial swelling.
Plan: Augmentin 625mg TDS x5/7, Flagyl 400mg TDS x5/7, Panadol 1g TDS (avoid NSAIDs - asthma). Refer dental clinic today for drainage +/- extraction. Return immediately if difficulty swallowing/breathing.

Doctor: What brings you in today?
Patient: Since Sunday I've had fever with shivering, and this side of my back is paining, the right side. I've vomited twice this morning.
Doctor: Any pain or burning when you pass urine?
Patient: Yes, it burns, and I'm going very often.
Doctor: When was your last period? Any chance you're pregnant?
Patient: It ended last week. No.
Doctor: We'll do the test anyway. ... Pregnancy test is negative. Your temperature is 39.1 and the pulse is fast. When I tap here on the right side of your back, it's very sore, isn't it?
Patient: Yes, very.
Doctor: Urine dip shows white cells, nitrites and blood. This is an infection that has gone up to the kidney, acute pyelonephritis. Malaria test is negative. I'm giving you the first dose of ceftriaxone injection here, and some fluids because you're vomiting. Then ciprofloxacin, five hundred twice a day for seven days. We'll send the urine for culture. If the vomiting continues or you feel worse, you'll need admission.

45M accountant. c/o heartburn and sour fluid coming up into the throat x3/12, mainly after heavy evening meals and when lying down. Sour taste in the mouth in the morning. Occasional dry cough at night.
No dysphagia, no odynophagia, no wt loss, no vomiting blood, no black stools.
SH: alcohol on weekends, non-smoker. BMI 31.
O/E: NAD. Abd soft, non-tender.
Ix: H. pylori stool Ag negative.
Imp: GORD (uncomplicated, no alarm features).
Plan: Esomeprazole 40mg OD before breakfast x8/52, Gaviscon 10ml after meals PRN. Elevate head of bed, last meal 3 hrs before sleep, wt loss. OGD if symptoms persist on PPI.

50F, known DM2 on metformin 1g BD, RBS 9.2 today. c/o R heel pain x2/12, worst with first steps in the morning, eases after walking. Tender medial calcaneal tubercle, no swelling. Foot pulses +, sensation intact. Imp: R plantar fasciitis. Plan: calf/plantar fascia stretches, heel cup, diclofenac gel, review 4/52.

16M Form 3 student, brought by father. c/o pimples on the face x1yr, worse in the last 3 months. Squeezes them.
O/E: Multiple inflamed papules and pustules over cheeks, forehead and chin, a few comedones. No nodules or cysts. Mild post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation. No scarring. Back clear.
Dx: Moderate papulopustular acne.
Plan: Benzoyl peroxide 5% gel nocte, clindamycin 1% gel mane, doxycycline 100mg OD x8/52. Gentle face wash, no squeezing. Review 8/52.

Doctor: Mzee, karibu. What's troubling you?
Patient: Daktari, at night I wake up four, five times to pass urine. And when I go, it takes a long time to start, and the flow is weak, it dribbles at the end.
Doctor: How long has this been going on?
Patient: Maybe one year, but it's worse now.
Doctor: Any blood in the urine, pain when passing, fever?
Patient: No blood, no pain.
Doctor: Any weight loss, bone pains?
Patient: No.
Doctor: I've examined the prostate through the back passage. It's enlarged, but smooth and not hard, and there are no lumps. Your PSA came back 2.1, that's within normal for your age, and the urine test is clean. The kidney function is fine. So this is a benign enlargement of the prostate, not cancer. I'm starting you on tamsulosin, one capsule at night. It can make you dizzy when you stand up, so get up slowly. Reduce tea and fluids after seven in the evening. Come back in six weeks and we'll see how the flow is.

38M driver, c/o bright red blood on tissue and dripping into the toilet after passing stool x3/52. Painless. Straining, hard stools, sits long hours. No change in bowel habit, no wt loss, no mucus. FHx nil.
O/E: Not pale. Abd soft. Perianal inspection: no fissure, no skin tags, no external swelling. DRE: no mass, no tenderness, soft stool, fresh blood on glove. Proctoscope not available today.
Hb 13.8.
Imp: Haemorrhoids (internal), grade not assessed.
Plan: Daflon 500mg 2 tabs BD, Anusol suppositories nocte x7/7, lactulose 15ml BD, high fibre diet, fluids. Refer surgical OPD for proctoscopy.

55M c/o sudden severe pain and swelling L big toe, woke him at 3am, after a wedding with nyama choma and beer. 1st MTP red, hot, exquisitely tender, can't bear the sheet. T 37.4. SUA 9.1 mg/dl. Imp: acute gout L great toe. Plan: colchicine 0.5mg BD x5/7, indomethacin 50mg TDS x3/7 with omeprazole, ice, cut red meat/alcohol. Allopurinol once settled.

24F c/o lower abdominal pain x5/7, fever, increased vaginal discharge, pain during sex. LMP 10/7 ago, regular. UPT negative. No urinary symptoms.
O/E: T 38.2, PR 98. Lower abdominal tenderness bilaterally, no rebound. Speculum: mucopurulent discharge from os. Bimanual: cervical motion tenderness +, bilateral adnexal tenderness, no mass.
PITC: negative. Urinalysis: NAD.
Dx: Acute PID.
Plan: Ceftriaxone 500mg IM stat, doxycycline 100mg BD x14/7, metronidazole 400mg BD x14/7. Partner notification slip given, abstain until both treated. Review 72hrs, admit if not improving.

Doctor: Tell me about this pain.
Patient: It's here, at the top of the stomach. It wakes me up at night, around two in the morning, and when I drink milk or take Eno it calms.
Doctor: How long?
Patient: About two months now. Sometimes it's worse when I'm hungry.
Doctor: Do you take any painkillers like Brufen or Diclofenac?
Patient: No, only Panadol sometimes for headache.
Doctor: Any vomiting of blood, black stool, losing weight?
Patient: No, nothing like that.
Doctor: Your tummy is tender just here in the middle top, but soft. Blood count is normal. With pain that wakes you at night and gets better with food, I think this is a peptic ulcer. We haven't confirmed if it's in the stomach or the duodenum, that would need a scope. The H. pylori test, the lab says the kit is out, so we'll do it next visit. For now omeprazole twice a day for eight weeks, avoid Brufen-type drugs, and stop the smoking if you can. If you get black stool or vomit blood, come straight back.

29F hairdresser. c/o itchy rash around the belly button x1/12 and on both ear lobes on and off for a year. Notices it's worse when she wears her jeans with a metal button and cheap earrings. No new soaps.
O/E: Well-demarcated lichenified eczematous plaque just below umbilicus corresponding to jeans stud; scaly erythema both ear lobes. Rest of skin clear.
Dx: Allergic contact dermatitis - nickel.
Plan: Betamethasone 0.1% cream BD x2/52 then taper, emollient. Cover metal buttons with tape/clear nail polish, surgical steel or gold earrings only.

6yo girl, review. Fever + dysuria + foul-smelling urine since last wk, started on amoxil. Urine c/s: E. coli >10^5 CFU/ml, R amoxicillin/co-trimoxazole, S nitrofurantoin/ceftriaxone. Afebrile today, no loin tenderness. Dx: UTI due to E. coli. Switch to nitrofurantoin x7/7, renal US booked.

35F teacher. c/o hard stools 2x/week x1yr, straining, sense of incomplete emptying, occasionally uses a finger to help. No abdominal pain, no bloating to speak of. No blood PR, no wt loss, no change in calibre. Not on iron or codeine. FHx: no bowel cancer.
O/E: Abd soft, non-tender, no masses. PR: hard stool in rectum, no mass, no fissure.
Ix: Hb 12.9, TSH normal, RBS 5.4.
Imp: Functional constipation (no alarm features, pain not a feature so not IBS).
Plan: Increase fibre/fluids, ispaghula husk sachet BD, lactulose 15ml nocte x2/52 then PRN, toilet routine after breakfast. Review 6/52.

58F DM2 on glibenclamide. R shoulder pain + stiffness x4/12, can't comb hair or fasten bra. Global loss of active AND passive ROM, ext rotation worst. XR shoulder normal. Imp: frozen shoulder R. Plan: physio referral, diclofenac 50mg BD x2/52, consider intra-articular steroid if no progress.

Doctor: Good morning. What can I do for you?
Patient: I have a discharge down there since Thursday, and it itches a lot, and it's a bit sore.
Doctor: What colour is it? Any smell?
Patient: Whitish-yellow, not much smell.
Doctor: Any pain in the lower tummy, fever, pain during sex?
Patient: No tummy pain. Sex is a bit sore because of the itching.
Doctor: When was your last period?
Patient: Two weeks ago. I'm on the injection.
Doctor: Okay. On examination the vaginal walls are red and inflamed with a thin discharge, the cervix looks healthy and there's no tenderness when I move it. The wet prep didn't show yeast or trichomonas. So it's an acute inflammation of the vagina, acute vaginitis. I'm giving you metronidazole tablets twice a day for a week and a clotrimazole pessary to cover. No alcohol with the metronidazole. Avoid douching and scented soaps. If it's not better in a week, come back and we'll take a swab for culture.

52M. C/o polyuria, nocturia x3/night and excessive thirst x2/12, ~6kg wt loss. No abdo pain, no vomiting. FHx: mother diabetic.
O/E: BMI 29.4, BP 128/82, no ketotic breath. Feet: pulses present, monofilament intact bilat. Fundi not seen (no ophthalmoscope today).
Ix: FBS 9.8 mmol/L, repeat 10.4. HbA1c 8.1%. Urinalysis glucose 2+, ketones neg. Creat 78.
Imp: T2DM, new dx. No complications found.
Plan: Metformin 500mg BD, titrate to 1g BD in 2/52. Diet & lifestyle counselling, lipid profile, refer eye clinic. R/v 4/52.

47F 2nd BP visit. Today 162/104, repeat 158/100 (2/52 ago 160/102). No headache/CP. No features of secondary cause, U/E normal, urine protein neg. Dx: HTN stage 2 – start Amlodipine 5mg OD, low salt diet, r/v 4/52.

Doctor: Good morning, what brings you in today?
Patient: I'm about two months pregnant and this morning I saw some blood when I went to the toilet.
Doctor: How much blood? Like a period or just spotting?
Patient: Just spotting, a little on the pad. And some cramps down here.
Doctor: Have you passed anything like clots or tissue?
Patient: No, nothing like that.
Doctor: Your last period was about nine weeks ago, and this is your second pregnancy, correct?
Patient: Yes, I have one child.
Doctor: I've examined you – the neck of the womb is closed and there's only a little blood. And on the scan here, see, the baby is inside the womb and the heart is beating, size matches nine weeks.
Patient: So the baby is okay?
Doctor: For now, yes. This is what we call a threatened miscarriage – there's bleeding but the pregnancy is continuing. Rest at home, no heavy lifting, no sex for a week or two. If the bleeding becomes heavy, or you pass clots, or the pain gets bad, come back immediately. I'll see you in one week with a repeat scan.

64M, known T2DM on glibenclamide 10mg BD + metformin 1g BD, also HTN on losartan 50mg.
Brought by son: sweating, shaking and confused this am after skipping breakfast (fasting for church). At triage GCS 15, slow to answer but oriented. RBS 2.6 mmol/L.
Given 50ml 50% dextrose IV -> RBS 7.8 at 15 min, symptoms resolved, eating.
BP 138/84, PR 92. Creat 140 (eGFR ~45) on last labs.
Imp: Low sugar episode 2' to sulphonylurea + missed meal, reduced renal clearance.
Plan: stop glibenclamide, continue metformin at reduced dose 500mg BD, add sitagliptin if needed at r/v. Hypo education given to pt and son (sugar/juice, carry sweets). Recheck HbA1c, U/E. R/v 1/52.

38F, 3/7 painful swollen L calf after 14-hr bus journey from Mombasa. On COC x2yrs. No CP, no SOB, no haemoptysis.
O/E: T 36.9, PR 88, SpO2 98% RA. L calf circumference 4cm > R, tender along deep veins, pitting oedema to knee. No superficial cord, no erythema.
UPT neg. Doppler US: non-compressible L popliteal and posterior tibial veins with echogenic thrombus.
Imp: Provoked L leg DVT (travel + oestrogen).
Plan: Rivaroxaban 15mg BD x21/7 then 20mg OD to complete 3/12. Stop COC – counselled, copper IUD offered. Warned re PE symptoms. R/v 1/52.
ANC revisit 29F G3P2 @ 24/40. Tired, dizzy on standing. Conj pale. Hb 8.9 g/dL, MCV 71. Dx: anaemia in pregnancy ?Fe def. IFAS 2 tabs OD, albendazole 400mg stat, diet advice, repeat Hb 4/52.

Doctor: You said you've been losing weight?
Patient: Yes, about eight kilos in three months, but I'm eating more than ever. I feel hot all the time, my hands shake, and my heart races.
Doctor: Any change in your periods?
Patient: They've become very light.
Doctor: Let me look at your neck... swallow for me. Your thyroid is enlarged all over, smooth, no lumps, and I can hear a bruit over it. Your eyes are also a bit prominent and you have a stare.
Patient: My sister said my eyes look different.
Doctor: Your results are back. TSH is suppressed, below 0.01, and free T4 is high at 48. Put together, this is Graves disease – your immune system is overstimulating the whole thyroid.
Patient: Is it curable?
Doctor: It can be controlled. I'm starting carbimazole 20 mg twice a day and propranolol 40 mg twice a day for the shaking and fast heart. We'll check a full blood count and thyroid tests in four to six weeks. If you get a sore throat or fever on carbimazole, stop it and come in the same day.

ANC: 31F G1P0 @ 34/40. C/o severe frontal headache + blurred vision since yesterday, epigastric pain this am. No fits. Booking BP 112/70 at 14/40.
O/E: BP 168/112, repeat 172/110. Facial + pedal oedema. Brisk reflexes, no clonus. FH 33cm, FHR 140s reg.
Urine protein 3+. Hb 11.8, plt 165 (point-of-care).
Imp: PET with severe features.
Plan: MgSO4 loading (4g IV + 10g IM), nifedipine 10mg PO, IV access, catheter for UO. Urgent ambulance referral to county referral hospital for stabilisation & delivery. Husband informed.

5yo boy, brought by teacher ~30 min after eating groundnut biscuits at a school party. Lip swelling, generalised hives, wheeze, vomited x2. No prior allergy hx.
O/E: anxious, RR 36, SpO2 91% RA, diffuse wheeze, BP 80/50, CRT 3s.
Mx: IM adrenaline 0.15mg ant thigh, repeated at 5 min; O2; NS 20ml/kg bolus; cetirizine; hydrocortisone IV.
30 min: SpO2 97%, BP 96/60, wheeze settling, hives fading.
Imp: Anaphylaxis – peanut.
Plan: observe 12 hrs, strict peanut avoidance, school informed, paeds allergy referral, adrenaline auto-injector discussed (availability/cost).

68M irregular heartbeat + mild SOB x1/52. Pulse irregularly irregular ~118, BP 134/86. ECG: AF, rate 115, no P waves, first time documented. TFTs pending. Dx: new AF. Bisoprolol 2.5mg, CHA2DS2-VASc 2 -> warfarin, INR 1/52, echo booked.

18mo girl. Mum reports poor appetite + 'swelling of the feet' x2/52. Weaned early onto mainly uji, recurrent diarrhoea last 2/12.
O/E: alert, bilateral pitting pedal oedema (+), thin sparse hair, flaky skin on legs. Wt 7.6kg, length 78cm, MUAC 11.0cm.
Appetite test: passed (ate RUTF). T 36.8, no dehydration, no fast breathing. HIV test neg (mother & child).
Imp: SAM, uncomplicated (oedema +, MUAC <11.5).
Plan: OTP enrolment, RUTF by weight band, amoxicillin x5/7, vit A per protocol, mum counselled on feeding. Weekly r/v at OTP.

Doctor: How has the breathing been since last month?
Patient: Worse, daktari. I now use three pillows, and I wake up at night gasping.
Doctor: And the legs?
Patient: Swollen up to here, the shoes don't fit.
Doctor: Are you taking the furosemide, the spironolactone and the enalapril every day?
Patient: Yes, but I sometimes skip the water tablet when I travel.
Doctor: Okay. Your neck veins are raised, I hear crackles at both lung bases, the swelling goes up to mid-shin and your liver is enlarged. Weight is up three kilos. Your blood pressure is 128 over 80.
Patient: Is the heart getting worse?
Doctor: The heart failure is congested again – fluid is building up in the lungs and the legs. We never managed to do the echo, so I'll book it. For now I'm increasing furosemide to 80 mg in the morning, keep spironolactone and enalapril, limit salt and fluids to about one and a half litres, and weigh yourself every morning. Come back in one week, sooner if the breathing is worse. Your blood pressure medicine for the hypertension stays the same.

First ANC visit. 22F G1P0, LMP 12/52 ago, sure of dates. Mild nausea, now resolved. No bleeding, no dysuria.
O/E: BP 108/68, wt 58kg, BMI 22. Uterus ~12/40 size.
ANC profile: Hb 12.4, O Rh+, VDRL non-reactive, HIV neg (PITC), HBsAg neg, urinalysis NAD, RBS 5.2.
Imp: single intrauterine pregnancy 12/40, primigravida, low risk.
Plan: IFAS, TT1, LLIN issued, birth preparedness & danger signs talk. Dating scan requested. Next ANC 20/40.
45M 'sugar check', father DM, occ thirst. ?DM. FBS 6.4, repeat 6.6 mmol/L; HbA1c 5.9%. Not diabetic. Dx: prediabetes – raised fasting sugar. Lifestyle, wt loss 5%, recheck FBS 6/12.

58M, known T2DM x8y on metformin + glimepiride (HbA1c 7.2% last month).
C/o central chest tightness on walking uphill / climbing stairs x4/12, relieved by rest in 3–5 min. Same pattern throughout, no pain at rest, no nocturnal pain. Non-smoker.
O/E: BP 136/84, PR 76 reg, HS1+2 no murmur, chest clear.
ECG: sinus rhythm, no ST/T changes. Pain-free today.
Imp: Exertional angina, stable pattern.
Plan: Aspirin 75mg OD, atorvastatin 40mg nocte, bisoprolol 2.5mg OD, GTN SL prn. Refer cardiology for stress test + echo. Continue DM meds. Return immediately if pain at rest or >15 min.

Doctor: Your sugar test results are here. Fasting was 5.6 and the two-hour value was 9.1.
Patient: Is that bad? I've never had sugar problems before.
Doctor: Before this pregnancy your sugar was normal – I see the check you had last year was fine. But these values show diabetes that has come with the pregnancy. You're twenty-six weeks now, which is when it usually shows up.
Patient: Will it harm the baby?
Doctor: If we control it, the risk is low. Uncontrolled, the baby can grow too big. First we start with diet – I'll send you to the nutritionist – cut down on sugary drinks, white bread and big portions of ugali. I'll give you a glucometer to check fasting and after meals. If the numbers stay high in two weeks, we'll add metformin.
Patient: Will I stay diabetic after delivery?
Doctor: Usually it goes away, but we'll repeat the test six weeks after you deliver, because you have a higher risk later in life.

45F c/o tiredness, cold intolerance, wt gain 5kg, constipation, heavy periods x6/12. TFTs normal 3 yrs ago (pre-employment). No neck surgery, no RAI, not on amiodarone/lithium.
O/E: dry skin, puffy face, slow-relaxing ankle jerks. No goitre. PR 58, BP 124/86.
Ix: TSH 28 mIU/L, FT4 6 pmol/L (low). Anti-TPO not done (cost).
Imp: Primary hypothyroidism, adult onset.
Plan: Levothyroxine 50mcg OD on empty stomach, repeat TSH 6/52, FBC for menorrhagia.

7yo F, fever 2/7 + painful R neck swelling. ?malaria – mRDT neg. Throat mildly injected. Single tender, warm 2.5cm R ant cervical LN, no fluctuance. Dx: acute R cervical lymph node infection. Augmentin 5/7, Panadol, r/v 3/7 or if fluctuant.

ANC: 27F G2P1 @ 22/40. Burning micturition, frequency, suprapubic discomfort x3/7. No fever, no loin pain, no PV discharge, no PV bleed.
O/E: T 36.8, renal angles non-tender, suprapubic tenderness mild. FH 22cm, FHR 148.
Urinalysis: nitrites +, leucocytes 3+, blood trace. Urine C/S sent.
Imp: Cystitis in pregnancy.
Plan: Cefalexin 500mg TDS x7/7, oral fluids, Panadol prn. Review with culture result. Repeat urine culture after treatment.

Patient: Doctor, I think it's my thyroid. I keep adding weight no matter what.
Doctor: I have the thyroid test result here – TSH is 2.1, completely normal. So it's not the thyroid.
Patient: Then why am I gaining?
Doctor: Let's go through your day. What do you eat?
Patient: Tea with bread in the morning, chapati and stew for lunch at the office, sometimes chips, and ugali at night. I sit all day at work.
Doctor: Any injections for family planning, or steroids, or other medicines?
Patient: No, nothing.
Doctor: Your weight is 92 kilos and height 1.65, so your BMI is about 34, which is in the obesity range. Waist is 102. Blood pressure is fine today.
Patient: So what do I do?
Doctor: The weight is from eating more than you burn and not moving much. I'll refer you to the nutritionist, aim for thirty minutes of brisk walking most days, cut the sugar in tea and the chips. I'm also checking fasting sugar and cholesterol because obesity raises those risks. Let's meet in three months.
